preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain owner privileges) to call includeInReward()
At least two addresses must be in the _excluded array
The address to be included (removed from exclusion) must be in the _excluded array

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, call includeInReward() on an excluded address that is NOT the last in the _excluded array. This will swap it with the last address but fail to update _excludedAddressToId for the swapped address, corrupting the mapping. Then call includeInReward() again on the corrupted address to cause array index issues or access wrong addresses.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The includeInReward function has a critical bug: when removing an address from the _excluded array, it swaps the last element into the removed position but fails to update the _excludedAddressToId mapping for the swapped address. This creates inconsistency where the mapping points to wrong indices, potentially causing array out-of-bounds access or incorrect state tracking in _getCurrentSupply() which iterates over _excluded array.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to gain privileges. 2. Create at least 3 excluded addresses to have a non-last element to target. 3. Call includeInReward on a middle element (not the last). 4. This corrupts the mapping for the swapped address. 5. Verify the corruption by checking that _excludedAddressToId[_excluded[lastIndex]] != 0 (should be 0 after proper removal).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call excludeFromReward on 3 different addresses to populate _excluded array. 3. Call includeInReward on the first excluded address (index 0). 4. This swaps the last address (index 2) to position 0 but doesn't update its mapping. 5. The mapping for the swapped address still points to index 2, but it's now at index 0. 6. The oracle check _excludedAddressToId[_excluded[lastIndex]] should be 0 but won't be.
